title: reading-notes-llm-inference-noah-williams
content:
Quick reading notes + takeaways from recent papers/blogs/conference talks on inference optimizations. Mostly for my own memory and to seed a short internal doc for the serving-runtime team. Informal - TODOs and open questions at the end.

High-level themes I'm tracking:
- Latency vs throughput tradeoffs: continuous batching + adaptive batching heuristics are still the most practical lever for reducing cost while hitting p95/p99 SLOs. Papers emphasize accepting a tiny latency increase in median to get large throughput wins.
- KV cache management: memory layout matters (contiguous memory for keys/values), and eviction/compaction strategies can reduce peak memory. Also important for multi-sequence serving and session-based chat.
- Quantization & accuracy: mixed results depending on model family and task. 8-bit/per-channel quantization + small calibration sets often preserves generation quality; 4-bit aggressive int8/4-bit techniques can work if paired with activation-scaling or small fine-tuning.
- Kernel fusion & attention optimizations: FlashAttention-style algorithms (tile + streaming from GPU memory) remain super beneficial, especially for long context lengths.

Notes on specific items I read this month:
1) "Efficient Transformer Inference: batching, caching and kernel choices" (arXiv/blog summary)
- Key idea: joint optimization across batching, KV cache layout, and kernel selection beats optimizing any one component alone.
- Practical: configure batching policies per-route (short vs long sequence workloads). For short chatty workloads, small batch sizes with aggressive prefix caching; for long single-shot completions, larger micro-batches + FlashAttention kernels.
- Implementation notes: need runtime profile feedback loop to pick kernel and batch size. Keep telemetry on token-level latency and tail percentiles.

2) "KV Cache Compaction and Eviction Strategies" (conference talk notes)
- Problem: multi-tenant systems see KV cache memory blow-up from many active sessions.
- Strategies discussed: LRU-like eviction of oldest session prefixes, compaction of contiguous KV blocks, and re-encoding older prefixes with lower precision.
- Takeaway: combine time-based eviction with workload-aware heuristics (e.g., keep last N tokens of active sessions; compress older tokens).

3) "Practical 4-bit Quant: recipe + pitfalls" (blog + code repo)
- Recipe: per-channel symmetric quant for weights, per-tensor for activations, calibrate on representative calibration set; keep layernorm and softmax in fp16/32.
- Pitfalls: outlier-sensitive layers (embedding and final layer) need special handling; generation quality regression on long-coherence tasks unless you keep some layers higher precision.
- Ops impact: reduces memory footprint substantially, but may increase compute overhead if emulation occurs on hardware without native support.

4) "Adaptive Batching for Low Tail Latency" (paper)
- Idea: dynamically adjust batching windows based on incoming request rate and observed queueing to meet latency SLOs.
- Implementation: maintain short adaptive window for low traffic; grow window when throughput is limited and latency still under SLO.
- Caveat: requires fast path for small-latency requests and robust fallback when kernel selection mismatches.

Concrete things I want to try in our runtime (experiments / POCs)
- Add a lightweight runtime profiler that records per-request: route, sequence length, model variant, kernel chosen, batch size, token-level latency. Use this to auto-suggest per-route batching policies.
- Implement KV cache compaction POC: when total KV size > threshold, compact oldest session blocks into fp16/8 and mark them as read-only; measure p99 impact.
- Evaluate mixed-precision per-layer: keep embedding/final layers in fp16 and quantize middle transformer blocks to 4-bit. Run on our internal eval set (code generation + long-dialog) to measure coherence delta.
- Small-scale adaptive batching: add a controller that grows/shrinks batching window using exponential backoff based on observed queue length / token latency.

Conference takeaways (notes from vendor talks + panels)
- Hardware trend: more commodity GPUs with better int8/4-bit prims are expected in next-gen clouds; need to keep abstraction so we can exploit hardware-specific fast paths.
- Observability matters: teams that instrument token-level metrics earlier can make better tradeoffs between cost and quality.
- Rollouts: gradual rollout + synthetic evals on prompt suites catch quality regressions from quantization.

Open questions / risks
- How to quantify small generation quality regressions in a way that stakeholders (product, customers) understand? Need a short rubric: metric + representative prompts + manual review threshold.
- Pricing/engineering trade: some kernels are faster but more expensive on cloud instance types; we need cost-aware routing.
- Multi-tenant cache fairness: ensuring hot sessions don't starve others - policy design question.

Action items (next 8 weeks)
- Week 1-2: implement minimal profiler + collect 2 weeks of traffic for the most-used model-route combo.
- Week 3-4: implement KV compaction POC (server-side only, feature-flagged). Run on shadow traffic.
- Week 5-6: run quantization experiments on internal eval set; collect automated metrics + small human pass.
- Week 7-8: integrate adaptive batching controller in staging and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per token.

Notes to self:
- Link back to runtime PRs and JIRA tickets as experiments progress (see linked_artifacts).
- Keep Aisha and Lena in loop - they have recent notes and eval harnesses.
- Write a short one-pager for product about what adaptive batching + KV compaction means for SLA/cost.

Random fragments / useful quotes I liked:
- "Small, targeted reductions in precision plus better caching often beat aggressive architecture changes."
- "Measure, don't guess - token-level telemetry is the single biggest enabler for production wins."

End of scratchpad.
